title: The Euclidean coefficient norm is a Euclidean norm pulled back by a continuous linear map
statement: Let P, n be natural numbers and Λ := Covector (Euclid P) n, the space of continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P. Let |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (∑_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2}, where (e_j) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P (EuclideanSpace.basisFun). Then there is a continuous linear map A : Λ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n → Fin P) with |α| = ‖A α‖ (Euclidean norm) for every α ∈ Λ.
lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), ∃ A : Covector (Euclid P) n →L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n → Fin P), ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖A α‖
